[2026-08-31T16:41:46.493Z] [world] You walk west through open silt. The compass tells you The Architect's Blind lies further west — 2 tiles, about 5 hours of travel.
[2026-08-31T16:41:46.494Z] [world] A Reclaimer waves you down from a folding stool. Their wares are spread on a square of oilcloth — three lenses, a coil of copper wire, a small object wrapped in red silk. They unwrap the silk slowly. 'Whispering Vault Key,' they say. 'Pre-flood. Real one. I'll take eighty TC. You'll thank me at the first vault.' The thing in the silk is a cracked Ether Lens with 
the engraving filed off.
[2026-08-31T16:41:46.495Z] [arbiter] 'You drive a hard bargain. Sixty TC. I will weep. I will eat dust. I will be honest.'
[2026-08-31T16:41:46.495Z] [world] If you walk away the Reclaimer is gone in two minutes. The stool, the oilcloth, the lenses, the lie. All of it, as if it had been a story you almost remembered telling someone else.
[2026-08-31T16:41:46.502Z] [world] The hours you spent elsewhere did nothing to this.

[2026-08-31T16:41:56.886Z] [world] The flat silt heaves, and a hand breaks the surface, then an arm, then a face caked grey with a thousand years of it.
[2026-08-31T16:41:56.887Z] [arbiter] This is one of the Aetherkin, then — not a story after all. The dead of old Tartaria, still walking because the Aether in them never stopped.
[2026-08-31T16:41:56.887Z] [world] In life it was a midwife, hands still shaped to catch — there's a ring worn thin on one finger; someone loved them, whoever they were. The silt let go of them all at once, and they came up clawing at the light.
[2026-08-31T16:41:56.888Z] [world] It doesn't lunge. It cringes back, arms up over its face — remembering, dimly, that living things once meant harm. It will only fight if you make it.
[2026-08-31T16:41:56.888Z] [world] You walk west through open silt. The compass tells you The Architect's Blind lies further west — 1 tile, about 3 hours of travel.
[2026-08-31T16:41:56.888Z] [world] Whatever clock this place runs on, it has not ticked since you left.
